title: Company Handbook — Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits & Onboarding
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This handbook page consolidates the most-requested people-ops guidance for engineers, product managers, and company builders at Redwood: role definitions, career ladder expectations, benefits and perks, the hiring + onboarding cadence, and the internal tools you’ll use daily. Use this page as the single source of truth for new hires and managers. For team-specific variations (e.g., Dedicated, SRE, Applied ML), consult the team’s hiring guide linked in Related Pages.

Key sections
- Roles & org overview
- Career ladders (IC & manager) — expectations, core competencies, and promotion guidance
- Hiring & onboarding (process + checklists)
- Benefits & perks (what to expect and how to enroll)
- Internal tools + quick access guide
- Contacts, escalation, and maintenance notes

Roles & Organization (high level)

Redwood’s core functional areas and typical role families:
- Engineering: Backend, Serving Runtime, Platform, Infra, SRE, DevX (SDKs/docs)
- Product: Product Managers, Design, Data & Applied ML product leads
- Research & Applied ML: model onboarding, evals, quantization profiles
- Go-to-market: Growth, Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering
- People Ops (HR): recruiting, compensation, learning & development
- Security & Compliance: audit, incident response, secure SDLC

For each hire, job postings and level expectations are owned by the hiring manager in partnership with People Ops. Team org charts live in the Team Wiki (see Related Pages).

Career Ladders: Principles and Paths

Principles
- Ladders are competency-based: promotion requires demonstrated impact across the rubric for the next level, not just tenure.
- Two parallel tracks: Individual Contributor (IC) and Manager. Transitioning between tracks requires evidence of the associated skills.
- Promotion cadence: typical promotion cycles are tied to quarterly calibration and the annual performance cycle; ad-hoc promotions are possible for exceptional impact.

Summary ladder table (example levels)
| Track | Level | Typical Title Examples | Core Focus |
|---|---:|---|---|
| IC | 1 | Software Engineer I / Associate PM | Learning & execution, shipping tasks with supervision |
| IC | 2 | Software Engineer II / PM II | Independent ownership of features, reliable delivery |
| IC | 3 | Senior Engineer / Senior PM | System design, cross-team influence, mentoring |
| IC | 4 | Staff Engineer / Principal PM | Technical leadership, architecture, strategic roadmap |
| Manager | M1 | Eng Manager / PM Manager | People management, delivery, team health |
| Manager | M2 | Senior Manager / Group PM | Multi-team planning, hiring, cross-org outcomes |

Competency buckets (used in calibration)
1. Execution & Delivery — shipping high-quality work on time.
2. Technical Craft / Product Judgment — design, architecture, data-informed decisions.
3. Collaboration & Influence — cross-team communication, stakeholder management.
4. Leadership & Mentorship — growing teammates, hiring, building culture.

Promotion guidance (practical steps)
1. Prepare a promotion packet: 1-page summary of impact, 3–5 project highlights, peer/manager feedback, metrics.
2. Discuss with manager at least one quarter before the promotion cycle.
3. Manager collects peer feedback and submits to the calibration committee per the Performance Calibration Guide.
4. Calibration committee reviews against rubric; outcome communicated within two weeks of the cycle close.

Hiring and Onboarding (end-to-end)

Hiring philosophy
- Hire for impact and culture add: technical skill plus ability to work in a fast-moving, production-first environment.
- Inclusive hiring: structured interviews, diverse panels, and consistent rubrics reduce bias.

High-level hiring process (steps)
1. Requisition & role profile: hiring manager drafts role + level, partners with People Ops for compensation band.
2. Sourcing & screening: recruiters source candidates; initial phone screen to assess fit.
3. Technical / role interviews: structured interviews with scoring rubric.
4. Final interview & bar check: hiring committee (includes cross-functional reps).
5. Offer & negotiation: People Ops handles comps and offer extension.
6. Pre-boarding: new hire paperwork, SSO invites, equipment requests.
7. Onboarding & ramp: 90-day onboarding plan owned by manager + buddy.

New-hire 90-day onboarding checklist (manager + new hire)
1. Before day 1:
   - Confirm equipment & account access (GitHub, Jira, Confluence, Slack, cloud console).
   - Add to relevant Google Groups and team calendar.
   - Share team wiki and 90-day plan.
2. Day 1:
   - Welcome meeting with manager and buddy.
   - Benefits enrollment overview with People Ops.
   - Security & compliance training assigned.
3. Week 1:
   - Core system walkthroughs: local dev environment, CI/CD, runbooks.
   - First small onboarding project assigned.
4. Month 1:
   - Cross-team introductions and customer-obs sessions.
   - 1:1 weekly cadence with manager established.
5. 30/60/90 check-ins:
   - 30-day: progress on basics and blockers.
   - 60-day: ownership of a feature or deliverable.
   - 90-day: ramp review and goals for next 6 months.

Buddy program
- Each new hire is paired with a buddy (peer-level) for the first 90 days to answer day-to-day questions and accelerate socialization. Managers are responsible for assigning a buddy before start date.

Benefits & Perks (how to enroll)

Health & financial benefits
- Medical, dental, and vision plans: multiple plan tiers with Open Enrollment each November. Enrollment via HRIS (link in Internal Tools).
- 401(k) with company match: match details in the Benefits Overview doc.
- Equity: RSUs or options depending on role and level; grant cadence described in Offer Letter.

Paid time off & leaves
- Vacation: flexible PTO policy; recommended minimum of 15 days/year for new hires.
- Sick leave: company policy aligned with regional law.
- Parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver policies; consult People Ops for eligibility and paperwork.
- Caregiver & bereavement leave: ad-hoc requests supported via People Ops.

Stipends & perks
- Home office stipend: one-time at hire + annual refresh.
- Wellness stipend: quarterly allowance for mental/physical wellness.
- Learning & development stipend: annual budget for conferences, courses, and books.
- Commuter benefits and public transit options (region-dependent).
- Team budgets for offsites and social events.

How to enroll / questions
- Primary enrollment: HRIS portal (link in Internal Tools). For questions, email people-ops@redwood.com.
- Benefits changes outside Open Enrollment: allowed for qualifying life events; submit request via HRIS.

Compensation philosophy
- Market-competitive salaries with leveling tied to role competencies and company stage. Total compensation = base + target bonus (where applicable) + equity. People Ops handles benchmarking and calibration.

Internal tools (quick access & common workflows)

Core accounts (provisioning + who to contact)
- SSO & Identity: Okta (contact it-support@redwood.com for access issues).
- HRIS & payroll: Rippling (benefits enrollment, payroll, time off).
- Communication: Slack (workspace and channels).
- Documentation: Confluence (this space).
- Code hosting: GitHub (org repo access via access request flow).
- CI/CD: Buildkite & internal runners.
- Observability & SLOs: Datadog / internal dashboards (access via Observability team).
- Ticketing / tracking: Jira (projects by team).

Common onboarding commands & links (examples)
- Accept device invite: follow IT email for laptop enrollment (macOS/Windows image).
- GitHub access request: https://github.com/orgs/redwood/teams -> request via People Ops if not auto-provisioned.
- Confluence: bookmark the Company Handbook and team wiki.
- CI queue: see Buildkite pipelines (team-runbooks -> onboarding).

Access & security guidelines
- Principle of least privilege: request minimum access needed; temporary elevated access must be timeboxed.
- Secrets & keys: use Vault/KMS and follow Secure SDLC docs in security-and-compliance.
- MFA required for all accounts.

Manager toolkit (hiring, onboarding, growth)
- Hiring: use the Hiring Requisition template in Confluence and coordinate with People Ops for interview panels.
- Onboarding: copy the 90-day plan template and adapt to role.
- Performance: quarterly 1:1s, calibration packets for promotion cycles, growth plans (career conversations).

FAQ & common troubleshooting
Q: Where do I request a new monitor or laptop?
A: Submit an IT ticket via the IT Self-Service Portal; include your manager in the approval flow.

Q: Who approves training budget?
A: Manager approval is required; People Ops will reimburse per the L&D policy.

Q: How do I add someone to an internal Slack channel?
A: Channel admins can add members; team leads may add for private channels.

Ownership, maintenance, and change log
- Owner: People Ops (Avery Chen) — responsible for periodic reviews and changes.
- Review cadence: annual review in Q4 plus ad-hoc updates for policy changes.
- How to propose changes: file a doc update request via Confluence inline comments or email people-ops@redwood.com.

Change log (high level)
- 2024-09-12: Initial consolidated handbook published.
- 2025-06-05: Added updated parental leave details and home office stipend.
- 2026-02-10: Clarified promotion packet requirements and revised onboarding checklist.

Appendix: Promotion packet template (copyable)
1. Candidate name, current role and level, proposed level
2. 1-paragraph summary of why promotion is recommended
3. Top 3–5 project summaries (what, impact, metrics, collaborators)
4. Leadership & mentorship examples (mentoring, hiring, knowledge sharing)
5. Risks & development goals post-promotion
6. Optional: peer feedback snippets (1–3)

Quick links (internal)
- HRIS / Benefits: https://hris.redwood.internal
- IT Self-Service: https://it.redwood.internal
- Hiring templates: /confluence/company-handbook/hiring-and-onboarding-templates
